title: Every day I get up at six
title_target: နေ့တိုင်း ခြောက်နာရီ ထပါတယ် — nay.-daiⁿ: hchowk-na-yee hta.-ba-dè
goal: Describe your daily routine — and clear up the biggest misunderstanding about Burmese: the ending တယ် is not a present-tense marker at all.
bekal: describe daily activities from getting up to going to bed
use the ending တယ် for real events, whenever they happen
use the ending မယ် for intentions and plans
negate with မ … ဘူး without forgetting either part
put time expressions in the right place

dialogs.title: စကားပြော — Telling Ko Zaw about her day
dialogs.intro: Ko Zaw asks Ani how she spends her day. Notice that sentences about **yesterday** and sentences about **every day** use the same ending, တယ်. The time is set by the words at the front of the sentence, not by the ending.

lines.speaker: ကိုဇော်:
lines.text: [အာနီ|a-nee]၊ [နေ့တိုင်း|nay.-daiⁿ:] [ဘယ်နှစ်နာရီ|bè-hna.na-yee] [ထ|hta.] [လဲ|lè:]။
lines.id: Ani, what time do you get up every day?

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [ခြောက်နာရီ|hchowk-na-yee] [ထ|hta.] [ပါတယ်|ba-dè]။ [ပြီးတော့|pyee:-dò.] [ရေချိုး|yay-hchoh:] [ပါတယ်|ba-dè]။
lines.id: I get up at six. Then I take a shower.
lines.literal: six-hour — get-up — polite-statement. after-that — water-pour — polite-statement.

lines.speaker: ကိုဇော်:
lines.text: [မနက်စာ|ma.nèk-sa] [ဘာ|ba] [စား|sa:] [လဲ|lè:]။
lines.id: What do you have for breakfast?

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [ဘာမှ|ba-hma.] [မစားဘူး|ma.sa:-boo:]။ [ကော်ဖီ|kò-hpee] [တစ်ခွက်|ta.hkwèk] [ပဲ|bè:] [သောက်|thowk] [ပါတယ်|ba-dè]။
lines.id: I don't eat anything. I just drink a cup of coffee.
lines.literal: anything — not-eat. coffee — one-cup — only — drink — polite-statement.

lines.speaker: ကိုဇော်:
lines.text: [အဲဒါ|è:-da] [မကောင်းဘူး|ma.kowⁿ:-boo:]။ [မနေ့က|ma.nay.-ga.] [ရော|yò:]။ [ဘာ|ba] [လုပ်|lohk] [လဲ|lè:]။
lines.id: That's not good. And yesterday? What did you do?
lines.literal: that — not-good. yesterday — how about? what — do — Q?

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [မနေ့က|ma.nay.-ga.] [ရုံး|yohⁿ:] [သွား|thwa:] [တယ်|dè]။ [ညနေ|nya.-nay] [ဈေး|zay:] [သွား|thwa:] [တယ်|dè]။
lines.id: Yesterday I went to the office. In the evening I went to the market.
lines.literal: yesterday — office — go — statement. evening — market — go — statement.

lines.speaker: ကိုဇော်:
lines.text: [ခဏ|hka.na.]၊ [မနေ့က|ma.nay.-ga.] [ဆိုပေမဲ့|hsoh-bay-mè.] [တယ်|dè] [ပဲ|bè:] [သုံး|thohⁿ:] [တယ်|dè] [နော်|nò]။
lines.id: Wait — it was yesterday, but you still used တယ်, right?
lines.literal: moment, yesterday — even-though — statement — just — use — statement — right.

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [ဟုတ်ကဲ့|hohk-kè.]၊ [မှန်|hmaⁿ] [လား|la:]။ [ကျွန်မ|cha.ma.] [မှား|hma:] [နေ|nay] [လား|la:] [လို့|loh.]။
lines.id: Yes — is that right? I thought I'd made a mistake.
lines.literal: true-yes, right — Q? I(f) — wrong — -ing — Q — (thought).

lines.speaker: ကိုဇော်:
lines.text: [မမှားဘူး|ma.hma:-boo:]။ [မြန်မာလို|myaⁿ-ma-loh] [တယ်|dè] [က|ga.] [အချိန်|a.hchayⁿ] [မ|ma.] [ပြော|pyò:] [ဘူး|boo:]။
lines.id: It's not wrong. In Burmese, တယ် doesn't say anything about time.
lines.literal: not-wrong. myanmar-way — statement — (topic) — time — not — say — not.

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [ဒါဆို|da-hsoh] [ဘာ|ba] [ကို|koh] [ပြော|pyò:] [လဲ|lè:]။

lines.speaker: ကိုဇော်:
lines.text: [တကယ်|ta.kè] [ဖြစ်|hpyik] [တာ|da] [ကို|koh] [ပြော|pyò:] [တယ်|dè]။ [မဖြစ်သေးရင်|ma.hpyik-thay:-yiⁿ] [မယ်|mè] [သုံး|thohⁿ:] [တယ်|dè]။
lines.id: It says something really happened. If it hasn't happened yet, you use မယ်.
lines.literal: really — happen — thing — (object) — say — statement. not-happen-yet-if — will — use — statement.

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [နားလည်|na:-lè] [ပါပြီ|ba-bee]။ [မနက်ဖြန်|ma.nèk-hpyaⁿ] [စောစော|sò-sò] [ထ|hta.] [မယ်|mè]!
lines.id: Got it. Tomorrow I'll get up early!
lines.literal: understand — polite-already. tomorrow — early — get-up — will!

grammars.title: ⚠️ တယ် is NOT a present-tense marker
body: Almost every beginner treats တယ် like the English present-tense "-s" or like "-ing". That's wrong, and the mistake will hold you back for months if it isn't straightened out now. **တယ် marks something real** — it has happened, it is the case, or it's a habit. The time is set by time words, not by the ending.

head: Sentence
Say it
Meaning
rows: (I) go to the office — time not stated
မနေ့က ရုံး သွားတယ်
အခု ရုံး သွားတယ်
မနက်ဖြန် ရုံး သွားမယ်

after: The dividing line isn't past versus present but **real versus not yet real**. Everything that has happened or simply holds true takes တယ်; everything that's still an intention, a plan, or a possibility takes မယ်.
The practical result is a relief: you **don't** need to learn any past-tense forms. Just put မနေ့က (yesterday) or ပြီးခဲ့တဲ့အပတ် (last week) at the front of the sentence, and you're done.

grammars.title: မယ် — intentions, plans, and offers
body: မယ် (*mè*) is the partner of တယ် for everything that hasn't happened yet. It covers "will", "going to", and "let me" all at once.

head: Burmese
Say it
Meaning
rows: မနက်ဖြန် သွားမယ်
ကျွန်တော် လုပ်ပါ့မယ်
ဘာ စားမလဲ

after: ⚠️ The **negative form is the same** for တယ် and မယ်: both become မ … ဘူး. မသွားဘူး can mean "don't go" or "won't go", and the context decides. That's a simplification in your favor — one negative form for all times.

grammars.title: Negation uses TWO parts
body: You've seen this pattern since unit 1; now it's time to use it without thinking. Burmese negation wraps the verb from both sides: **မ** in front and **ဘူး** after.

head: Statement
Its negative
Say it
rows: မကောင်းဘူး
မသွားပါဘူး

after: ⚠️ If the sentence uses ပါ, then ပါ stands **between** the verb and ဘူး: မသွားပါဘူး. Putting it anywhere else sounds wrong immediately. For "not … anything", use ဘာမှ … မ … ဘူး: ဘာမှ မစားဘူး (I don't eat anything).

grammars.title: Time words go at the FRONT
body: Since the ending doesn't express time, time words carry the whole job — and their place is always at the start of the sentence, before the subject or right after it.

head: Burmese
Say it
Meaning
rows: တစ်ခါတစ်လေ
ဘယ်တော့မှ မ…ဘူး

after: ⚠️ တိုင်း (*daiⁿ:*) means "every" and attaches at the back: နေ့တိုင်း (every day), အပတ်တိုင်း (every week), နှစ်တိုင်း (every year). Once again the marker comes after — a pattern that shouldn't surprise you anymore.

sections.title: A day from getting up to going to bed

blocks.text: The verbs in this list cover almost an entire ordinary day. Try telling your own day out loud with this list, using the ending တယ်, then repeat it with မနေ့က at the front — and notice that the verbs don't change at all.

head: Burmese
Say it
English
rows: ရေချိုးတယ်
သွားတိုက်တယ်
မနက်စာ စားတယ်
အလုပ် လုပ်တယ်
နေ့လယ်စာ စားတယ်
အိမ် ပြန်တယ်
ချက်ပြုတ်တယ်
တီဗွီ ကြည့်တယ်

blocks.title: The three-sentences-a-day drill
items: Starting today, write **three sentences** about your day before bed: one with မနေ့က, one with ဒီနေ့, one with မနက်ဖြန်. The third will use မယ်; the first two use တယ်.
Three sentences a day until you finish this book means sixty sentences you built yourself — worth far more than sixty pages you only read.

items: မယ် / ထ / စောစော / မနက်ဖြန်
Every day I get up at six.
Yesterday I went to the market.
In the evening I go home.
